'''Christine L. Mummery''' (born March 29, 1953) is an appointed professor of Developmental Biology at [[Leiden University]] and the head of the Department of Anatomy and Embryology at [[Leiden University Medical Center]] in the Netherlands.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lumc.nl/org/anatomie-embryologie/medewerkers/902201040032533?setlanguage=English|title=Christine L. Mummery PhD {{!}} LUMC|last=LUMC|website=www.lumc.nl|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-12-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/staffmembers/c.l.-mummery|title=C.L. Mummery|website=Leiden University|language=en|access-date=2019-12-12}}</ref>

Prof. Mummery has pioneered studies on [[Cardiac muscle cell|cardiomyocytes]] from [[Embryonic stem cell|human embryonic stem cells]] (hPSC)<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mummery Christine|last2=Ward-van Oostwaard Dorien|last3=Doevendans Pieter|last4=Spijker Rene|last5=van den Brink Stieneke|last6=Hassink Rutger|last7=van der Heyden Marcel|last8=Opthof Tobias|last9=Pera Martin|last10=de la Riviere Aart Brutel|last11=Passier Robert|date=2003-06-03|title=Differentiation of Human Embryonic Stem Cells to Cardiomyocytes|journal=Circulation|volume=107|issue=21|pages=2733–2740|doi=10.1161/01.CIR.0000068356.38592.68|pmid=12742992|doi-access=free}}</ref> and was among the first to inject them in mouse heart after [[myocardial infarction]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van Laake|first1=Linda W.|last2=Passier|first2=Robert|last3=Monshouwer-Kloots|first3=Jantine|last4=Verkleij|first4=Arie J.|last5=Lips|first5=Daniel J.|last6=Freund|first6=Christian|last7=den Ouden|first7=Krista|last8=Ward-van Oostwaard|first8=Dorien|last9=Korving|first9=Jeroen|last10=Tertoolen|first10=Leon G.|last11=van Echteld|first11=Cees J.|date=2007-10-01|title=Human embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes survive and mature in the mouse heart and transiently improve function after myocardial infarction|journal=Stem Cell Research|volume=1|issue=1|pages=9–24|doi=10.1016/j.scr.2007.06.001|pmid=19383383|issn=1873-5061|doi-access=}}</ref> Mummery was the first to derive human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC) in Netherlands and is leading in their use for cardiovascular disease modelling and safety pharmacology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.monash.edu/pharm/about/events/SCDMDD/speakers/christine-mummery|title=Christine Mummery|website=Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences|language=en|access-date=2019-12-12}}</ref> In 2010, she established the LUMC hiPSC [[core facility]].<ref>[https://www.lumc.nl/research/facilities/hipsc-core-facility/ Webpage LUMC hiPSC core facility]</ref>

== Early education and career ==
Mummery obtained a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[Physics]], [[Electronics]] and [[Mathematics]] in 1974 from the [[University of Nottingham]], UK. Prof. Mummery completed her Ph.D. in Biophysics from the [[University of London|University of London, UK]] for researching the effect of ultrasound in wound healing at [[King's College London]] in 1978.<ref>C.L.Mummery (1978). The effect of ultrasound on fibroblasts 'In Vitro'. [https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.466566 British Library Ethos page]</ref>

== Research and career ==
From 1978 to 1980, Mummery worked as a Postdoctoral fellow at the [[Royal Society]], UK working on ''"Ion transport, differentiation and the cell cycle in neuroblastoma cells”''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mummery|first1=C. L.|last2=Boonstra|first2=J.|last3=van der Saag|first3=P. T.|last4=de Laat|first4=S. W.|date=July 1982|title=Regulation of the cell cycle in neuroblastoma cells: the role of ion transport|journal=Cell Biology International Reports|volume=6|issue=7|pages=654|doi=10.1016/0309-1651(82)90129-1|doi-broken-date=14 September 2025 |issn=0309-1651|pmid=6290085}}</ref> In 1981, she continued with a Postdoctoral fellowship at the [[Hubrecht Institute]] ([[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences|KNAW]]), Utrecht, working on neuroblastoma and embryonal carcinoma cells as screens for teratogens<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mummery|first1=C. L.|last2=Brink|first2=C. E. van den|last3=Saag|first3=P. T. van der|last4=Laat|first4=S. W. de|date=1984|title=A short-term screening test for teratogens using differentiating neuroblastoma cells in vitro|journal=Teratology|language=en|volume=29|issue=2|pages=271–279|doi=10.1002/tera.1420290213|pmid=6740511|issn=1096-9926}}</ref> before being appointed tenured staff scientist working on developmental biology, differentiation and stem cells in 1985. In 1993, Prof. Mummery became a group leader working on [[Transforming growth factor beta|TGFβ]] and BMP signalling in mouse development using cardiomyogenesis and [[vasculogenesis]] in mouse and human (embryonic) stem cells as models. In 2007, Mummery was a visiting professor jointly at the [https://hsci.harvard.edu/ Harvard Stem Cell Institute (HSCI)] and the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study|Radcliffe Institute]] working on to engineer cardiac grafts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/christine-mummery|title=Christine Mummery|date=2012-03-16|website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University|language=en|access-date=2019-12-12}}</ref>

Prior to her position as Chair of the Department of Anatomy and Embryology at [[Leiden University Medical Center]], Prof. Mummery was a professor of [[Developmental biology|Developmental Biology]] at the [[Faculty of Medicine]], [[Utrecht University|University of Utrecht]] from 2002 to 2008.

Since 2015, Mummery is a Professor of Vascular Modelling at the Technical University of Twente to develop organ-on-chip models.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.utwente.nl/en/news/2019/7/257132/demonstrating-the-potential-of-organ-on-chip|title=Demonstrating the potential of 'organ-on-chip' {{!}} Home (EN)|website=Universiteit Twente|language=en|access-date=2019-12-12}}</ref>  

Prof. Mummery is also the co-founder of LUMC spinout Pluriomics bv (now Ncardia<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://ncardia.com/ |title = Home}}</ref> since September 2017)

Mummery is a [[Board of directors|board member]] of the [[Hubrecht Institute]] ([[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences|KNAW]]), the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]] and the  [https://www.isscr.org/ International Society of Stem Cell research (ISSCR)] from which she is vice president since 2018 until 2020.

Mummery is also the founding [[Editing|editor]] of [[Stem Cell Reports]]; is on the [[Editorial board|editorial Board]] of [[Cell Stem Cell]]s, [[Stem Cells (journal)|Stem Cells]], [http://www.currentstemcellresearchtherapy.com/ Current Stem Cell Res. and Therapy], [[Cardiovascular Research]], [[Molecular Therapy]] & [[Differentiation (journal)|Differentiation]]. She is in the Scientific Advisory Boards of EU IMI StemBANCC, Galapagos, Pluripotent Stem Cell Initiative (UK).

== Awards and honours ==
* ISSCR Public Service Award 2023 <ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.isscr.org/isscr-news/christine-l-mummery-receives-the-2023-isscr-public-service-award | title=Christine L. Mummery Receives the 2023 ISSCR Public Service Award }}</ref>
* Elected member [[Academia Europaea]] (2015)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Mummery_Christine |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328142645/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Mummery_Christine |title=Christine Mummery |publisher=Academia Europaea |date= |archive-date=28 March 2019}}</ref>
* Hans Bloemendaal Medal 2014 for innovative interdisciplinary research
* Hugo van de Poelgeest Prize 2014 for Animal Alternatives
* Elected member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) (elected 2010)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5453 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191118095111/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5453 |title=Christine Mummery |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=18 November 2019}}</ref>
* Radcliffe Fellowship, Harvard University (2007)
* Royal Society Fellowship, UK (1978, 1979)

== Books ==
Mummery co-authored “Stem Cells, 2nd edition ''scientific facts and Fiction''” (Elsevier 2014).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mummery |first1=Christine |last2=Stolpe |first2=Anja van de |last3=Roelen |first3=Bernard |last4=Clevers |first4=Hans |title=Stem Cells: Scientific Facts and Fiction |date=2014 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-411567-5 |url=https://www.elsevier.com/books/stem-cells/mummery/978-0-12-411551-4 }}</ref> This second edition contains introduction to embryonic and iPS cells and stem cells. It also features additional information on "organs on chips" and adult progenitor cells.
